record.original_question: Let n be a positive integer written in base 2, and let S(n) be the sum of the binary digits of n. Is the asymptotic density of the set of positive integers n for which S(n^2) is even equal to 1/2? This item is explicitly marked solved in the source: the proof notes state that the problem is a special case of Theorem 3 of Christian Mauduit and Joël Rivat.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, write $n$ in base $2$ and let $S(n)$ denote the sum of its binary digits. Determine whether the set
$$\{n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} : S(n^2) \text{ is even}\}$$
has natural (asymptotic) density equal to $1/2$. That is, prove or disprove that
$$\lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\,\#\{1 \le n \le N : S(n^2) \equiv 0 \pmod{2}\} = \frac{1}{2}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Gelfond problem on the parity of the binary digit sum of squares. It was resolved affirmatively by Christian Mauduit and Joël Rivat, who proved more generally that the digits of $n^2$ in any base $q\ge 2$ are equidistributed in arithmetic progressions ("La somme des chiffres des carrés", Acta Math. 203 (2009), 107–148). In particular the density equals $1/2$.

status_evidence.title: La somme des chiffres des carrés — Mauduit & Rivat
status_evidence.snippet: Mauduit and Rivat resolved Gelfond's conjecture on the sum of digits of squares, proving equidistribution in arithmetic progressions; in particular S(n^2) is even for a set of density 1/2.
status_evidence.claim: The Gelfond problem on the parity of S(n^2) is solved with density 1/2.
